name: Lauren Underwood
page_title: Lauren Underwood's Issue Positions (Political Courage Test)
on_the_ballot: Running, Democratic for U.S. House (IL) - District 14

positions.question: Do you support the Supreme Court's decision to overturn Roe v. Wade?

evidence.text: "I am disgusted by the plans that Republican lawmakers have laid out to impose a federal ban on abortion care and overturn other legal precedents that protect our civil rights. Our lives will change radically, even those of us in states like Illinois."

"The ultra-conservative Court’s opinions in this ruling make clear that our civil rights are broadly under threat — everything from who we can marry, to which Americans are protected from illegal discrimination is now at risk."

"Today is a dark day for women and Americans across the nation. The Supreme Court just struck down our constitutional right to privacy and bodily autonomy. In the history of our country, Americans have never, ever, lost a constitutional right. Unfortunately, that's now no longer true. Abortion became illegal in at least 13 states today — often with no exceptions for rape and incest. This marks a shameful moment in our country's history — a day that will always be remembered as the moment the Supreme Court ripped away a woman's right to make decisions about her body and conservatives across the country criminalized health care. This activist Supreme Court is clearly ruling to meet the demands of an extremist minority of Americans. There must be court reform to restore public trust and confidence in their role of ensuring equal justice under the law."

"Six Supreme Court justices, who are completely out of step with the American people, ripped away Americans’ reproductive rights. We won’t go back. I’m fighting for a reality where women aren’t criminalized for getting health care and providers aren’t prosecuted for doing their jobs. Republican lawmakers across the country are trying to ban abortion — often without exception. My Democratic colleagues and I voted to pass this legislation to reinstate a federal right to abortion and guarantee that Americans can’t be prosecuted for seeking care in states where abortion remains legal."

"Social Security and Medicare are worth defending, strengthening, and protecting for generations to come."
"🚨 House Republicans’ new plan would cut Social Security benefits for nearly 10 million Illinois residents."

positions.question: Do you support protecting government officials, including law enforcement officers, from personal liability in civil lawsuits concerning alleged misconduct?

evidence.text: "Americans have demanded their communities be made safer. The George Floyd Justice in Policing Act delivers urgently needed reforms to require body cameras, ban chokeholds, and create a national database of police misconduct. It’s now time for the Senate to pass this bill."

"Since the events of last summer, millions of Americans have demanded their communities be made safer for everyone. Safe communities and accountable policing go hand in hand, and the George Floyd Justice in Policing Act delivers urgently needed reforms."
"We have seen too many lives taken and communities devastated by police brutality and racial injustice. Action is long overdue."
Voted in favor of HR 1280 "George Floyd Justice in Policing Act of 2021"

positions.question: Do you support the federal government taking action, beyond those of the Federal Reserve, to alleviate inflation?

evidence.text: "Fantastic news — my bill, the Health Care Affordability Act, has been included in the Inflation Reduction Act! If passed, the Inflation Reduction Act will extend the tax credits from my bill that have helped lower out-of-pocket premium costs by an average of $2,400 per family."

"The Inflation Reduction Act is now law! This historic law addresses the most critical issues we face today and lowers the cost of health coverage and prescription drugs, tackles our climate crisis, and fights inflation."

positions.question: Do you support the forgiveness of federal student loan debt?

"For too many Americans, college is unaffordable and student debt in our country is at a crisis level. As a country, we need to ensure all young people have the choice to obtain affordable higher education without the burden of back-breaking loan debt after graduation."

"Student debt is a barrier for millions of people who are hoping to start a family, own a home, start a business, and save for retirement. If you’re struggling with debt, there are options for relief."

positions.question: Do you support government funding for the development of renewable energy (e.g. solar, wind, geo-thermal)?

evidence.text: "My community is already experiencing the effects of climate change. I passed the Inflation Reduction Act, the single largest climate investment in our history, to prevent the worst effects of climate change. Because it's not a future threat — it’s an immediate one."

"Climate change is an emergency that demands urgent, bold action. The Build Back Better Act is historic legislation that will tackle the climate crisis while investing in our competitiveness and creating clean energy jobs to power our future."

"We must take action to create a clean and bright future for young people everywhere. Hear from my Youth Transportation Advisor, Rowan, on how the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law will invest in clean energy solutions and build a brighter future for generations to come."

"We’re driving into a clean energy future in my community! The Bipartisan Infrastructure Law is helping manufacturers like Lion Electric expand our fleet of electric school buses. I’m beaming with pride that this work is happening right in Joliet."

positions.question: Do you generally support gun-control legislation (e.g. red flag laws, boyfriend loopholes)?

evidence.text: "Enough is enough. Our gun violence crisis must end. When I voted to pass the Assault Weapons Ban, I thought of the senseless tragedies that have touched too many communities, and how this legislation will help protect future generations from violence."

"Gun violence is preventable, and yet, it’s such a tragically routine occurrence in this country that every community has a story. Mine is no exception. Recently, I strongly supported the passage of two bipartisan, commonsense solutions to address our nation’s gun violence crisis."

"In 2019, five of our neighbors left their homes to go to work at the Henry Pratt Company and never returned because of an unspeakable act of gun violence — a senseless tragedy for their families and our community. And now, just three years later, I am continuing to hear from my constituents who are heartbroken over the countless mass shootings in this country and fearful that their community could experience the same tragedy that took place in Aurora. Whether it's at school, work, a concert, a place of worship, or their own home, everyone deserves to feel safe. I took action to reduce our country's horrific gun violence crisis by voting to pass the Protecting Our Kids Act."
Voted in favor of HR 1446 "Enhanced Background Checks Act of 2021"

positions.question: Do you support a government-run (e.g. single-payer) healthcare program, such as Medicare-for-All?

evidence.text: ".@ewarren and I have the same belief: everyone deserves quality, affordable healthcare. So honored to be endorsed by Senator Warren and @TeamWarren, and proud to have a partner to lower healthcare costs for working families"

"AS A REGISTERED NURSE, PUBLIC HEALTH EXPERT, AND A WOMAN WITH A PRE-EXISTING HEART CONDITION, LAUREN’S NUMBER ONE PRIORITY IN CONGRESS IS ENSURING ACCESS TO HIGH-QUALITY, AFFORDABLE HEALTH CARE FOR OUR FAMILIES AND ELIMINATING COST BARRIERS TO CARE."

"As part of her work to eliminate cost barriers to health care, Lauren wrote the Health Care Affordability Act with her constituents top of mind. Signed into law as part of the American Rescue Plan, and later extended through the Inflation Reduction Act, the Health Care Affordability Act limits the cost of health care coverage for people who choose Marketplace plans to eight and a half percent or less of their income. This law has proven to be so popular, over 16 million Americans signed up for health care coverage in 2022, with 4 in 5 enrollees finding a plan for $10 or less per month."

"In Illinois, African Americans are 5x more likely to die from COVID-19. We can’t assume people will come to a healthcare system where there may be mistrust or long-standing barriers & expect positive outcomes. We must meet people where they are & provide quality, affordable care."

positions.question: Do you support expanding paid family AND/OR medical leave benefits (e.g. maternity leave)?

evidence.text: "Health care. Reproductive rights. Paid family leave. Equal pay. Affordable childcare. These aren't Democratic or Republican, male or female issues. They're human issues. We're ready to bring humanity back to government."

"Providing a strong economic footing for women in Illinois is one of my top priorities in Congress. I introduced a Women’s Economic Agenda: focused on a paid family leave policy, access to affordable healthcare, and closing the gender pay gap for women."

"Women and families shouldn’t have to choose between paying the bills and taking care of someone they love. I admire these women for sharing their stories. It’s time we implement a national paid family leave program."

"Women now outnumber men in our workforce. We must have programs in place to support the realities of being a woman in the workforce, our economy depends on it. We are fighting for national paid family leave, affordable child care, equal pay, & our reproductive rights."

positions.question: Should the government be able to regulate the cost of prescription drugs?

evidence.text: "Lauren responded to skyrocketing insulin prices with the bipartisan Lower Insulin Costs Now Act. The legislation was signed into law by President Trump in 2019, to make lower-cost, generic insulin available more quickly. Now, insulin costs are now capped at $35/month for seniors on Medicare."
Voted in favor of HR 3 "Lower Drug Costs Now Act of 2019"
Voted in favor of HR 5378 "Lower Costs, More Transparency Act"
